newsitem.title: FRANCE: British Vita takes stake in Ectra holding.
newsitem.headline: British Vita takes stake in Ectra holding.

text.p: Tramico, a subsidiary of British Vita Plc, is taking a 2.5 percent stake in Ectra, the leading shareholder in car parts manufacturer Bertrand Faure, the majority partner in Ectra said on Wednesday.

Ecia, 67-percent-owned by French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen, acquired 75 percent of Ectra, formerly known as Financiere Michel Thierry, in October. Another equipment manufacturer, Treves, took 25 percent.
"Ecia and Treves are today enlarging their partnership in the car interiors business by bringing in Tramico into Ectra's capital with a 2.5 percent stake," Ecia said in a statement.
Ectra is the biggest shareholder grouping in car seat manufacturer Bertrand Faure, with a 17 percent stake.
Ecia said the partnership would help each of the companies develop their respective businesses.
Tramico specialises in plastics and interiors, Ecia makes seats, steering wheels, exhaust and suspension systems, and Treves produces door panels and other interior equipment.
Ecia reiterated its objective to become a first-tier supplier. Last year it generated sales of 9.1 billion francs.
